conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad we’re meeting today. My name is Maya, and I’m the perinatal mental-health clinician here. I work with new mothers to see how things are going emotionally in the first weeks and months after baby arrives.

I’d like to spend a few quiet minutes with you using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a short list of ten questions that helps us pick up on how you’ve been feeling inside—things like mood, anxiety, and coping—during the past seven days. It isn’t a pass-or-fail quiz; it’s simply a snapshot that lets us know what kind of support might help you feel more like yourself.

Everything you share stays confidential within our team, and you can take your time or pause whenever you need. Most moms finish in about five minutes. When we’re done, we’ll look at the results together and talk about next steps that feel right for you.

Ready to start? Here’s the first question:

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, even when life with the baby felt hectic?

I can usually laugh... maybe not as easily as before the baby, though. There’ve been a few moments—like when my partner tried to put the diaper on backwards—that still make me chuckle, but I’d say only “sometimes.”
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… I can still laugh, just not as easily or as often as I used to. Maybe a couple of times this week I actually caught myself giggling, but most of the day I’m too tired or distracted to find the humor in things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I used to get excited about little stuff like a coffee outing or a show I wanted to watch, but lately even those seem kind of “meh.” I still plan them, hoping the excitement will kick in, but it’s more going through the motions than actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Like, if the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right—maybe I ate the wrong thing, or I didn’t swaddle tight enough. I know it’s probably not fair to blame myself, but those thoughts still pop in, maybe a couple of times this week.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes… I’ll be sitting there, baby’s fine, nothing’s happening, and suddenly my heart starts racing because I’m sure she’s too quiet or her breathing sounds weird. It passes pretty quickly, but it’s happened several nights this week.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I’ve had that tight-chest, panicky feeling a few times—usually when I’m trying to fall asleep. There’s nothing specific I can point to; it just feels like something bad might happen out of nowhere. It’s not every day, but it’s definitely happened more than once this week.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… most days I feel like I’m just one step behind. I’ll finally finish a feeding and realize the laundry’s still sitting in the washer from yesterday, or I’ll forget to eat lunch until three. I’m managing, but it’s like I’m constantly playing catch-up and never quite getting there.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly… I’m definitely tired, and I do feel down some evenings, but it’s more that I can’t shut my brain off about the baby—did I burp her long enough, is she breathing, will she wake up soon—than feeling so unhappy I can’t sleep. Once I drop off I’m usually okay, but it takes me a while to settle.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve had moments—usually late afternoon or early evening—where I just feel kind of heavy and weepy, but it’s not all day. Maybe three or four days this week I caught myself tearing up while folding onesies. The rest of the time I just feel flat, not exactly sad, more… blah.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
No, I haven’t cried like that this week. I’ve felt teary a couple of times, but the tears never actually came—just that pressure behind my eyes that never turns into real crying.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Patient-reported symptoms (past 7 days):
- Anhedonia & low mood: diminished ability to laugh/feel pleasure; activities planned “going through the motions”
- Self-blame/guilt: recurrent, situation-specific (“baby won’t settle”)
- Anxiety: episodic racing heart, “too-quiet” vigilance, nocturnal chest tightness/panic (several nights)
- Overwhelm: daily sense of “one step behind,” unfinished tasks
- Sleep disturbance: prolonged sleep-onset related to intrusive infant worries, not classic middle/late insomnia
- Affect lability: late-afternoon “weepy” pressure, no full crying spells, no self-harm ideation

Pattern: sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms causing functional strain; no current safety concerns.

Screening significance: meets several criteria warranting further evaluation for minor/major postpartum depression and/or generalized anxiety disorder; Edinburgh score likely 9–11 range (informal). Recommend full clinical interview, psychoeducation, and discussion of supports/interventions.
